raw_response:
I have been growing cotton on this land for 40 years, so I know what works here. Quzhou soil is mostly loam, slightly alkaline, and the well water is reliable but salty if I pump too deep. With 12 mu and just my wife and me, I need varieties and a schedule I can actually manage without too much hired labor.

I will plant a Bt hybrid again — last few years I used 国欣棉 series and got around 280 kg seed cotton per mu. Bollworm pressure is lower since everyone around here uses Bt, but I still spray for aphids, mirid bugs, and spider mites — those have gotten worse since Bt came in. I count on 7 sprays through the season.

For fertilizer, I follow what I worked out years ago and adjust to current prices. Cotton needs more potassium than people think — I learned that the hard way when bolls were small in the dry years. I apply about 15 kg N per mu (split: half as base with compound fertilizer before planting, the rest as topdressing at squaring and flowering), 7 kg P₂O₅, and 10 kg K₂O. I use a 15-15-15 compound as base, then urea for topdressing. I also throw in some farmyard manure on about 4 mu where I can haul it.

Irrigation: I water before planting (mengshui), then once at squaring, once at peak flowering, once at boll-filling if July is dry. So 3-4 times depending on rain. I plough deep every other year to break the pan; this year is a plough year.

12 mu is enough that I think about cost per mu carefully but I will not skimp on potassium or the squaring topdressing — that is where yield comes from.
